$comment: ATSC A/85 is a Recommended Practice, not a standard in the shall-sense: section 6 says 'should' throughout, and its target applies specifically to content delivered or exchanged WITHOUT metadata and with no prior arrangement between the parties. The constraints below carry that qualification; a spec that departs from them has departed from the recommended practice it names.
name: ATSC A/85

document.title: ATSC A/85 — Techniques for Establishing and Maintaining Audio Loudness for Digital Television

assets.audio.loudness.standards[].target.cite: §6 Target loudness and true peak levels for content delivery or exchange
assets.audio.loudness.standards[].target.quote: For delivery or exchange of content without metadata (and where there is no prior arrangement by the parties regarding loudness), the Target Loudness value should be –24 LKFS.
assets.audio.loudness.standards[].target.note: LKFS and LUFS are the same unit under different names (EBU R 128 footnote 1); UMDP records the number, and the standard's name says which convention it is stated in.

assets.audio.loudness.standards[].tolera.quote: Minor measurement variations of up to approximately ±2 dB about this value are anticipated, due to measurement uncertainty, and are acceptable (due to the comfort zone - see Annex E). Content loudness should not be targeted to the high or low side of this range.
assets.audio.loudness.standards[].tolera.note: ±2 dB is a measurement-uncertainty band, not licence to aim off target — A/85 says so in the same breath. A stricter house tolerance is inside the practice; a looser one is not.

assets.audio.loudness.true_peak_max.quote: The true-peak level should be kept below -2 dB TP in order to provide headroom to avoid potential clipping due to downstream processing (such as audio coding used in delivery).
assets.audio.loudness.true_peak_max.note: The ceiling exists to leave coding headroom, so a lower one is squarely in the spirit of the practice.
